title: Use data-analytics outputs to identify notable items — Ferris Components
instructions: The engagement team ran journal-entry tests and a margin visualization over Ferris Components' full-year general ledger (a private company). Performance materiality is $150,000. Review the outputs and decide how the team should respond.

exhibits.title: Journal-entry test results
exhibits.content:
| Test | Entries flagged | Total amount | Notes from the data |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| 1. Manual entries to revenue posted after the period-end close | 5 | 640,000 | All by the controller; descriptions "true-up" |
| 2. Entries posted by users without posting authority | 3 | 412,000 | Users in the warehouse department |
| 3. Entries posted on Saturday or Sunday | 14 | 86,000 | All posted by user SYS-BATCH (nightly scheduled job) |
| 4. Round-dollar entries over $50,000 | 9 | 1,250,000 | Monthly depreciation and prepaid amortization |

exhibits.title: Gross margin visualization
exhibits.content:
Monthly gross margin ran between **37% and 39%** from January to November and rose to **46%** in December. Drilling down shows that the December increase comes almost entirely from sales to **Halden Supply**, a new customer invoiced on December 28–30 under **bill-and-hold** terms; the goods remain in Ferris's warehouse.

The recurring depreciation and amortization schedules were tested earlier and agree to approved fixed-asset and prepaid records.

parts.prompt: For each output, select the most appropriate response.
options: Investigate every flagged item: inspect support and inquire of someone other than the preparer
Refine the test parameters and rerun before investigating
No further investigation: the flags are explained by corroborated, expected activity

rows.label: Test 1 — manual entries to revenue posted after the period-end close
rows.answer: Investigate every flagged item: inspect support and inquire of someone other than the preparer
rows.explanation: Post-close manual revenue entries are a classic management-override indicator, and revenue carries a presumed fraud risk (AU-C 240). Every entry is examined.

rows.label: Test 2 — entries posted by users without posting authority
rows.answer: Investigate every flagged item: inspect support and inquire of someone other than the preparer
rows.explanation: These indicate an access-control failure. Each entry is examined for validity and support, and the access deficiency is evaluated.

rows.label: Test 3 — entries posted on weekends
rows.answer: Refine the test parameters and rerun before investigating
rows.explanation: All 14 were posted by the scheduled nightly batch user. The test was not designed to exclude system-generated entries, so refine it and rerun to find any manual weekend entries.

rows.label: Test 4 — round-dollar entries over $50,000
rows.answer: No further investigation: the flags are explained by corroborated, expected activity
rows.explanation: All nine agree to approved recurring depreciation and amortization schedules that the auditor has already tested.

rows.label: Visualization — December gross margin 46% vs. 37–39% in other months
rows.answer: Investigate every flagged item: inspect support and inquire of someone other than the preparer
rows.explanation: An unexpected spike driven by one new customer on bill-and-hold terms is a notable item; test every December sale to that customer against the bill-and-hold criteria and cutoff.

parts.prompt: Identify the area most directly affected by each finding.

rows.label: Test 1 — post-close manual revenue entries
rows.explanation: Entries recorded after the close that increase revenue bear on whether the revenue occurred in the period.

rows.label: Test 2 — unauthorized users posting entries
rows.explanation: Users posting without authority point to a failure of logical access controls, which affects the reliability of all system data.

rows.label: Bill-and-hold sales to the new customer
rows.explanation: Revenue is recognized only when control transfers; bill-and-hold arrangements must meet specific criteria.
